papers.title: Wastewater-Based Surveillance of Human Papillomavirus Genotype Diversity
papers.abstract: Importance Human papillomaviruses (HPVs) account for more than 30% of infection-related cancers worldwide. Surveillance of circulating HPV genotypes at the population level remains limited because clinical monitoring primarily relies on cervical screening and does not capture infections in men or individuals outside screening programs. Objective To assess whether wastewater-based epidemiology can monitor the diversity and temporal circulation of HPV genotypes at the population level. Design, Setting, and Participants This is a cross-sectional study of raw wastewater collected twice weekly from January 24, 2024, to January 29, 2025, at a large wastewater treatment plant serving approximately 1 million population equivalents in the Paris, France, metropolitan area. Exposure Population-level shedding of HPV DNA into wastewater. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were detection frequency, diversity, and temporal patterns of HPV genotypes in wastewater. HPVs of the genus Alphapapillomavirus were quantified using a broad-spectrum quantitative polymerase chain reaction assay and normalized using human-associated excretion markers (crAssphage and mitochondrial DNA). Twenty-eight HPV genotypes were screened using a multiplex polymerase chain reaction assay. Detection reproducibility was evaluated with McNemar tests (mid-P method); quantification reproducibility was evaluated using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for censored data. Results HPVs were detected in all 100 wastewater samples analyzed, with a mean concentration of 7.3 × 10 3 genome equivalents/L (range, 7.3 × 10 1 to 3.0 × 10 5 genome equivalents/L), showing moderate temporal variability over the study period. Twenty-seven HPV genotypes were identified, with a median of 6 genotypes per sample (range, 1-12). The most frequently detected genotypes were HPV-66 (97%; 95% CI, 93%-100%), HPV-6 (93%; 95% CI, 88%-97%), and HPV-53 (89%; 95% CI, 83%-95%). High-risk HPV-39 and HPV-56, which are not covered by current vaccines, were detected in 72% (95% CI, 63%-81%) and 58% (95% CI, 48%-68%) of samples, respectively, vs 21% (95% CI, 13%-29%) for HPV-16 and 5% (95% CI, 1%-10%) for HPV-18, both of which are vaccine targeted. Temporal modeling showed relatively stable viral circulation over the study period. Conclusions and Relevance In this cross-sectional study of wastewater collected from a large urban population, wastewater-based epidemiology enabled population-level monitoring of HPV genotype circulation and complemented clinical surveillance by capturing infections across sexes and age groups. These findings suggested that this approach may facilitate evaluation of the effectiveness of HPV vaccination programs and serve as a scalable tool for monitoring HPV genotype diversity within the population.

Surveillance of circulating HPV genotypes at the population level remains limited because clinical monitoring primarily relies on cervical screening and does not capture infections in men or individuals outside screening programs. Objective To assess whether wastewater-based epidemiology can monitor the diversity and temporal circulation of HPV genotypes at the population level. Design, Setting, and Participants This is a cross-sectional study of raw wastewater collected twice weekly from January 24, 2024, to January 29, 2025, at a large wastewater treatment plant serving approximately 1 million population equivalents in the Paris, France, metropolitan area. Exposure Population-level shedding of HPV DNA into wastewater. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were detection frequency, diversity, and temporal patterns of HPV genotypes in wastewater. HPVs of the genus Alphapapillomavirus were quantified using a broad-spectrum quantitative polymerase chain reaction assay and normalized using human-associated excretion markers (crAssphage and mitochondrial DNA). Twenty-eight HPV genotypes were screened using a multiplex polymerase chain reaction assay. Detection reproducibility was evaluated with McNemar tests (mid-P method); quantification reproducibility was evaluated using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for censored data. Results HPVs were detected in all 100 wastewater samples analyzed, with a mean concentration of 7.3 × 10 3 genome equivalents/L (range, 7.3 × 10 1 to 3.0 × 10 5 genome equivalents/L), showing moderate temporal variability over the study period. Twenty-seven HPV genotypes were identified, with a median of 6 genotypes per sample (range, 1-12). The most frequently detected genotypes were HPV-66 (97%; 95% CI, 93%-100%), HPV-6 (93%; 95% CI, 88%-97%), and HPV-53 (89%; 95% CI, 83%-95%). High-risk HPV-39 and HPV-56, which are not covered by current vaccines, were detected in 72% (95% CI, 63%-81%) and 58% (95% CI, 48%-68%) of samples, respectively, vs 21% (95% CI, 13%-29%) for HPV-16 and 5% (95% CI, 1%-10%) for HPV-18, both of which are vaccine targeted. Temporal modeling showed relatively stable viral circulation over the study period. Conclusions and Relevance In this cross-sectional study of wastewater collected from a large urban population, wastewater-based epidemiology enabled population-level monitoring of HPV genotype circulation and complemented clinical surveillance by capturing infections across sexes and age groups. These findings suggested that this approach may facilitate evaluation of the effectiveness of HPV vaccination programs and serve as a scalable tool for monitoring HPV genotype diversity within the population.

papers.title: Safety and Immunogenicity of First Russian Quadrivalent (Recombinant, Adsorbed) Human Papillomavirus (Types 6, 11, 16, 18) Vaccine in Children Aged 9–17 Years: Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Blind, Phase III Clinical Trial
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a significant risk factor for the development of HPV-associated precancerous and malignant diseases. Recombinant adsorbed vaccine against HPV (types 6, 11, 16, and 18) has been developed in Russian Federation to prevent these conditions. Vaccine immunogenicity and safety have been studied in adults. The aim of the study is to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of Russian recombinant adsorbed quadrivalent vaccine against HPV (types 6, 11, 16, and 18) in children aged 9–17 years in comparison to reference quadrivalent vaccine. Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, phase III clinical trial with a 1 : 1 participant allocation ratio. The study included healthy seronegative children aged 9–17 years. Study participants aged 9–13 years received either the investigational vaccine or the reference vaccine. Vaccine safety was assessed from April 2, 2024 to April 14, 2025, in all participants who received at least one vaccine dose (as-treated population). Any post-vaccination reactions and adverse events (AE) were recorded, their correlations with vaccination, severity, and duration were evaluated. The primary efficacy endpoint was the geometric mean titer ratio (GMT Ratio) of antibodies to HPV 1 month after full vaccination course (Per-Protocol (PP) population); additionally, the GMT Ratio was evaluated for every HPV type. Randomization was centralized and based on computer-generated list. Allocation concealment was ensured via the method of sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes. A total of 705 AEs were registered during the study period, 426 of which were considered related to vaccination. No severe vaccination-related AEs were reported. The investigational vaccine demonstrated comparable immunogenicity to the reference drug across all four HPV types in both age cohorts. The seroconversion rate in PP population ranged from 97% to 100%. Higher GMT values were observed in participants aged 9–13 years compared to those aged 14–17 years. GMT values were higher in the investigational drug group in both age cohorts for HPV type 18. Favorable safety profile and adequate immunogenicity of the investigational vaccine were recorded compared to the reference vaccine in children aged 9–17 years. The obtained data suggest that the investigational vaccine is a promising drug for HPV-associated diseases prevention.

papers.title_zh: 9-17岁儿童中第一种俄罗斯四价(重组、吸附)人乳头瘤病毒(6、11、16、18型)疫苗的安全性和免疫原性:多中心、随机、双盲、III期临床试验
papers.source_body_en: Human papillomavirus (HPV) infection is a significant risk factor for the development of HPV-associated precancerous and malignant diseases. Recombinant adsorbed vaccine against HPV (types 6, 11, 16, and 18) has been developed in Russian Federation to prevent these conditions. Vaccine immunogenicity and safety have been studied in adults. The aim of the study is to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of Russian recombinant adsorbed quadrivalent vaccine against HPV (types 6, 11, 16, and 18) in children aged 9–17 years in comparison to reference quadrivalent vaccine. Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, phase III clinical trial with a 1 : 1 participant allocation ratio. The study included healthy seronegative children aged 9–17 years. Study participants aged 9–13 years received either the investigational vaccine or the reference vaccine. Vaccine safety was assessed from April 2, 2024 to April 14, 2025, in all participants who received at least one vaccine dose (as-treated population). Any post-vaccination reactions and adverse events (AE) were recorded, their correlations with vaccination, severity, and duration were evaluated. The primary efficacy endpoint was the geometric mean titer ratio (GMT Ratio) of antibodies to HPV 1 month after full vaccination course (Per-Protocol (PP) population); additionally, the GMT Ratio was evaluated for every HPV type. Randomization was centralized and based on computer-generated list. Allocation concealment was ensured via the method of sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes. A total of 705 AEs were registered during the study period, 426 of which were considered related to vaccination. No severe vaccination-related AEs were reported. The investigational vaccine demonstrated comparable immunogenicity to the reference drug across all four HPV types in both age cohorts. The seroconversion rate in PP population ranged from 97% to 100%. Higher GMT values were observed in participants aged 9–13 years compared to those aged 14–17 years. GMT values were higher in the investigational drug group in both age cohorts for HPV type 18. Favorable safety profile and adequate immunogenicity of the investigational vaccine were recorded compared to the reference vaccine in children aged 9–17 years. The obtained data suggest that the investigational vaccine is a promising drug for HPV-associated diseases prevention.
papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染是与HPV相关的癌前病变和恶性疾病发生的重要风险因素。在俄罗斯联邦开发了重组吸附型疫苗疫苗,以预防这些疾病。疫苗在成人中的安全性和免疫原性已得到研究。本研究旨在评估俄罗斯重组吸附型四价疫苗疫苗在9-17岁儿童中针对HPV(6、11、16、18型)的安全性和免疫原性,并与参考四价疫苗疫苗进行比较。该研究是一项多中心、随机、双盲、平行组、III期临床试验,采用1:1的受试者分配比例。研究纳入了9-17岁健康的HPV血清阴性儿童。9-13岁的受试者接受了试验用疫苗或参考疫苗。从2024年4月2日至2025年4月14日,对所有至少接受一次疫苗疫苗的受试者(按治疗人群)评估了疫苗的安全性。记录了所有与疫苗接种疫苗相关的反应和不良事件(AE),并评估了其与疫苗接种疫苗的相关性、严重程度和持续时间。主要疗效终点是完成全疗程疫苗接种疫苗后1个月针对HPV的抗体几何平均滴度比值(GMT Ratio)(符合方案人群);此外,每种HPV类型的GMT Ratio也被评估。随机化通过计算机生成的列表进行,并通过依次编号、不透明、密封的信封方法确保了分配遮蔽。在研究期间共注册了705例不良事件(AE),其中426例被认为与疫苗接种疫苗相关。未报告严重的疫苗接种相关AE。试验用疫苗在9-13岁和14-17岁两个年龄段中,针对所有四种HPV类型均表现出与参考药物相当的免疫原性。在符合方案人群中,血清转换率范围为97%至100%。9-13岁组的GMT值高于14-17岁组。在两种年龄组中,针对HPV 18型,试验用药物组的GMT值均高于参考药物组。与参考疫苗相比,试验用疫苗在9-17岁儿童中表现出良好的安全性和足够的免疫原性。获得的数据表明,试验用疫苗可能是预防HPV相关疾病的一种有前景的药物。

papers.title: A unique initiative: Human papillomavirus vaccination for girls in Assam, India
papers.abstract: Abstract: The first human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination initiative was undertaken in Assam, with an indigenously made vaccine in India, “CERVAVAC,” in association with a nonprofit organization during March 2025–February 2026. The main objective was to initiate HPV vaccination among girls from 9 years and above to create widespread awareness and prevent cervical cancer. A total of 2000 girls received the vaccine with a total of 3800 doses. Persistent infection with high-risk HPV genotypes is the principal etiological factor for cervical cancer, and prophylactic vaccination can prevent up to 90% of cases. A survey in Assam showed less that 1% had previously vaccinated against HPV, and awareness was 39% among students of elite academic institutions due to lower socioeconomic status, population heterogeneity, and deeply rooted sociocultural beliefs significantly contributing to less screening and vaccination coverage. Nongovernmental organizations played a pivotal role in spreading awareness and vaccination all over India, but this vaccination drive was the first initiative in the state of Assam. The impact was an infinite transformation of mindset to a finite measurable outcome, setting a national record of highest vaccination by a nongovernmental organization within 1 year time.
papers.journal: Annals of Oncology Research and Therapy

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the lack of HPV vaccination programs in Assam, India, by initiating a unique initiative to vaccinate girls aged 9 years and above to prevent cervical cancer and raise awareness about HPV-related diseases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a vaccination initiative conducted in Assam, India, from March 2025 to February 2026, targeting girls aged 9 years and above. A total of 2000 girls received the vaccine, with 3800 doses administered.
analysis.methods: The initiative involved administering an indigenously made HPV vaccine, CERVAVAC, in collaboration with a nonprofit organization. The study focused on raising awareness and promoting vaccination among girls in the target population.
analysis.main_results: A survey revealed that less than 1% of girls in Assam had previously been vaccinated against HPV, and awareness was 39% among students of elite academic institutions due to factors such as lower socioeconomic status, population heterogeneity, and sociocultural beliefs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrated that sociocultural and economic factors significantly influenced HPV vaccination coverage and awareness, highlighting the need for targeted awareness campaigns in low-resource settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of addressing sociocultural barriers to improve HPV vaccination rates and cervical cancer prevention in regions with limited healthcare access.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single state and the use of survey data rather than clinical outcomes. However, the evidence is strong as it provides insights into the challenges of HPV vaccination in Assam, India.

analysis.summary_en: This study describes the first HPV vaccination initiative in Assam, India, using the indigenously made vaccine CERVAVAC. The main objective was to increase vaccination rates and awareness among girls aged 9 years and above to prevent cervical cancer. A survey found that less than 1% of girls had previously been vaccinated, and awareness was 39% among students of elite institutions due to socioeconomic and cultural factors. The initiative highlighted the role of nongovernmental organizations in promoting vaccination and awareness. The study's findings emphasize the need for culturally sensitive strategies to improve HPV vaccination coverage in low-resource settings. However, the study is limited by its focus on a single state and reliance on survey data rather than clinical outcomes, which affects the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过为9岁及以上女孩开展独特的疫苗接种计划,解决印度阿萨姆邦缺乏HPV 疫苗接种项目的现状,以预防宫颈癌并提高对HPV相关疾病的认识。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项在印度阿萨姆邦开展的疫苗接种计划,时间为2025年3月至2026年2月,针对9岁及以上女孩。总计有2000名女孩接受了疫苗疫苗,共接种了3800剂。
elements_zh.methods: 该计划涉及与一家非营利组织合作,为9岁及以上女孩接种印度本土研发的HPV 疫苗疫苗“CERVAVAC”。研究重点是提高目标人群女孩对HPV相关疾病的意识并推广疫苗接种。
elements_zh.main_results: 调查结果显示,阿萨姆邦不到1%的女孩曾接种过HPV疫苗,而精英学术机构的学生中仅有39%有相关意识,这归因于较低的社会经济地位、人口异质性以及根深蒂固的社会文化观念。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究表明,社会文化和经济因素显著影响了HPV 疫苗接种的覆盖率和意识水平,强调了在资源匮乏地区开展针对性意识宣传活动的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果突显了应对社会文化障碍以提高HPV 疫苗接种接种率和宫颈癌预防措施的重要性,特别是在医疗资源有限的地区。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于仅针对一个州,并且基于调查数据而非临床结果。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它提供了关于印度阿萨姆邦HPV 疫苗接种接种挑战的见解。

papers.title: Prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus infection among women undergoing HPV testing at a hospital in Zhangzhou, China: a retrospective study
papers.abstract: Introduction This retrospective, single-center study aims to analyze the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in women undergoing HPV testing at a hospital in Zhangzhou, China. Methods A total of 13,492 females, 18–85 years, undergoing HPV testing at the physical examination center of a hospital in Zhangzhou, China, were recruited. Cervical cast-off cells were collected for HPV testing by low-density gene chip and flow hybridization technology using HPV typing test kit. A total of 27 kinds of HPV types were detected using this method, including 17 kinds of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) and 10 kinds of low-risk/uncertain oncogenic significance HPV (LR-HPV). Results The overall HPV infection rate was 16.86% (2,275/13,492), with 12.59% (1,699/13,492) females detected as single HPV-type infection and 4.27% (576/13492) females detected as multiple HPV-type infection. Among all 27 detected HPV types, HPV52 exhibited the highest prevalence (3.58%, 483/13,492), followed by HPV53 (1.76%, 237/13,492) and HPV81 (1.71%, 231/13,492). The most common HPV coinfection pattern was HPV52 + HPV53 (12/2,275). Overall HPV prevalence showed a “two-peak” age-related distribution, with the first peak in the ≤29-year age group (19.69%) and the second peak in the ≥60-year age group (24.45%), respectively. It decreased in the 40- to 49-year age group (13.64%). The prevalence of single/multiple HPV and HR-HPV/LR-HPV infection also exhibited age-related trends similar to those described above. Binary logistic regression analysis revealed a non-linear relationship between HPV prevalence and age ( p < 0.05). Conclusion Our study revealed the basic genotype- and age-specific distribution of HPV infection among females attending the physical examination center of a hospital in Zhangzhou. These results emphasized that the specific population should strengthen regular HPV surveillance and improve awareness of vaccination, especially for the highly prevalent HPV types (HPV52,53,51). In addition, our findings provide valuable insights for the measurement of HPV prevention interventions.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to analyze the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in women undergoing HPV testing at a hospital in Zhangzhou, China, to provide insights into the epidemiological patterns of HPV in this population.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective, single-center study was conducted on 13,492 females aged 18–85 years who underwent HPV testing at the physical examination center of a hospital in Zhangzhou, China.
analysis_en.methods: Cervical cast-off cells were collected for HPV testing using low-density gene chip and flow hybridization technology. Binary logistic regression analysis was performed to assess the relationship between HPV prevalence and age.
analysis_en.main_results: A total of 27 HPV types were detected, including 17 high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) and 10 low-risk/uncertain oncogenic significance HPV (LR-HPV). The overall HPV infection rate was 16.86% (2,275/13,492), with 12.59% (1,699/13,492) being single HPV-type infections and 4.27% (576/13,492) being multiple HPV-type infections. The prevalence of HPV showed a "two-peak" age-related distribution, with peaks in the ≤29-year and ≥60-year age groups.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study revealed the basic genotype- and age-specific distribution of HPV infection among females in Zhangzhou, highlighting the need for targeted surveillance and awareness of vaccination for the most prevalent HPV types.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings provide valuable insights for the measurement of HPV prevention interventions and emphasize the importance of regular HPV surveillance in this population, particularly for the highly prevalent HPV types.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is retrospective and based on a single-center sample, which may limit generalizability. However, the evidence is strong as it is based on direct HPV testing and statistical analysis of a large cohort.

papers.title_zh: 患病率和人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)感染在福建省漳州市医院接受人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)检测的女性中的基因型分布:一项回顾性研究
papers.source_body_en: Introduction This retrospective, single-center study aims to analyze the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in women undergoing HPV testing at a hospital in Zhangzhou, China. Methods A total of 13,492 females, 18–85 years, undergoing HPV testing at the physical examination center of a hospital in Zhangzhou, China, were recruited. Cervical cast-off cells were collected for HPV testing by low-density gene chip and flow hybridization technology using HPV typing test kit. A total of 27 kinds of HPV types were detected using this method, including 17 kinds of high-risk HPV (HR-HPV) and 10 kinds of low-risk/uncertain oncogenic significance HPV (LR-HPV). Results The overall HPV infection rate was 16.86% (2,275/13,492), with 12.59% (1,699/13,492) females detected as single HPV-type infection and 4.27% (576/13492) females detected as multiple HPV-type infection. Among all 27 detected HPV types, HPV52 exhibited the highest prevalence (3.58%, 483/13,492), followed by HPV53 (1.76%, 237/13,492) and HPV81 (1.71%, 231/13,492). The most common HPV coinfection pattern was HPV52 + HPV53 (12/2,275). Overall HPV prevalence showed a “two-peak” age-related distribution, with the first peak in the ≤29-year age group (19.69%) and the second peak in the ≥60-year age group (24.45%), respectively. It decreased in the 40- to 49-year age group (13.64%). The prevalence of single/multiple HPV and HR-HPV/LR-HPV infection also exhibited age-related trends similar to those described above. Binary logistic regression analysis revealed a non-linear relationship between HPV prevalence and age ( p < 0.05). Conclusion Our study revealed the basic genotype- and age-specific distribution of HPV infection among females attending the physical examination center of a hospital in Zhangzhou. These results emphasized that the specific population should strengthen regular HPV surveillance and improve awareness of vaccination, especially for the highly prevalent HPV types (HPV52,53,51). In addition, our findings provide valuable insights for the measurement of HPV prevention interventions.

papers.title: Parental perception and intention to vaccinate female children 9–14 years with the human papillomavirus vaccine in Ile-Ife, Nigeria: theory of planned behaviour approach
papers.abstract: Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is a highly effective strategy for preventing cervical cancer; however, achieving high vaccination coverage among eligible girls depends largely on parental decision-making. This study assessed parental perceptions and intention to vaccinate female children aged 9–14 years against HPV in Ile-Ife, Nigeria, using the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB). A cross-sectional study was conducted between August and September 2024 among 163 parents of female children aged 9–14 years attending selected secondary schools in Ile-Ife, Nigeria, using a multistage sampling technique. Data were collected using a pretested questionnaire developed from previously validated instruments and analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 27. Chi-square tests and multivariable logistic regression were performed to identify factors associated with parental intention to vaccinate at a significance level of p < 0.05. Of the 163 questionnaires distributed, 160 (98.2%) were completed and analysed (response rate: 98.2%). Overall, 59.4% of parents had a positive perception of HPV vaccination, while 60.6% expressed an intention to vaccinate their female children. Higher education level (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 6.06; 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.11–17.38) and perceived behavioural control (AOR = 11.97; 95% CI 4.69–30.56) were associated with parental intention to vaccinate. In conclusion, both positive perception of HPV vaccination and parental intention to vaccinate female children were suboptimal. Perceived behavioural control and parental educational level were significant predictors of parental intention to vaccinate. Interventions aimed at strengthening parental intention should therefore give attention to these factors.

papers.abstract_zh: 人乳头瘤病毒(人乳头瘤病毒,HPV)疫苗接种是预防宫颈癌的一种高度有效的策略;然而,实现对符合条件的女孩的高疫苗接种覆盖率在很大程度上取决于父母的决策。本研究采用计划行为理论(TPB)评估了在尼日利亚伊莱-伊费为9-14岁女性儿童接种HPV疫苗的父母看法和意愿。2024年8月至9月期间,采用多阶段抽样技术,在尼日利亚伊莱-伊费的163名9-14岁女性儿童的父母中进行了一项横断面研究。数据通过预先测试的问卷收集,该问卷基于先前验证的工具开发,并使用IBM SPSS Statistics版本27进行分析。进行了卡方检验和多变量逻辑回归分析,以确定与父母接种意愿相关因素,显著性水平为p < 0.05。共发放了163份问卷,其中160份(98.2%)被完成并分析(回复率:98.2%)。总体而言,59.4%的父母对HPV 疫苗接种有积极看法,而60.6%的父母表达了为女性儿童接种疫苗的意愿。较高的教育水平(调整后比值比[AOR] = 6.06;95%置信区间[CI] 2.11–17.38)和感知行为控制(AOR = 11.97;95% CI 4.69–30.56)与父母接种意愿相关。总之,父母对HPV 疫苗接种的积极看法和为女性儿童接种疫苗的意愿均不理想。感知行为控制和父母的教育水平是父母接种意愿的重要预测因素。因此,旨在加强父母接种意愿的干预措施应关注这些因素。

papers.title: Development and Psychometric Validation of the Human Papillomavirus Prevention Health Literacy Scale for College Students in Taiwan.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted virus associated with several types of cancer. Because college students are a high-risk group, understanding their health literacy with regard to HPV prevention is critical. However, no suitable measurement tools are currently available for this purpose. PURPOSE: In this study, an HPV Prevention Health Literacy Scale (HPV-HLS) was developed, and its reliability and validity were assessed. METHODS: A cross-sectional design was used, and the developed scale was validated on a sample of 372 college students from two universities in northern Taiwan and one university in central Taiwan. The initial scale comprised 49 items, developed from qualitative interviews and a literature review. After content validity assessment and item analysis, the scale was refined to 37 items. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted with 150 participants, followed by confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with 222 participants. Concurrent validity and internal consistency reliability were assessed. Data were collected from November 2021 to December 2022. RESULTS: The results of the EFA revealed a two-factor model accounted for 60.30% of the total variation, and those of the CFA demonstrated favorable goodness-of-fit indices (GFI = .81, CFI = .92, TLI = .91, RMSEA = .07, and SRMR = .02). Moreover, the average variance extracted (AVE) for the two factors were .56 and .64, respectively, with corresponding composite reliability (CR) values of .96 and .93, indicating excellent convergent validity. Notably, the AVE surpassed the squared product-moment correlation of the corresponding factors, affirming good discriminant validity. The final iteration of the HPV-HLS comprised 21 items with two subscales: comprehension and evaluation of general information and seeking information from health care professionals. Concurrent validity was found between the proposed scale and the Mandarin Multidimensional Health Literacy Questionnaire ( r = .68, p < .001). The HPV-HLS demonstrated good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .959). CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS FOR FUTURE PRACTICE: After rigorous psychometric testing, the newly developed HPV-HLS demonstrated excellent reliability and validity, establishing it as an objective tool for evaluating HPV prevention health literacy among college students. This HPV-HLS may be used by health care providers and educators to assess health literacy and evaluate the effectiveness of clinical interventions to prevent HPV infection.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and validate a psychometric tool, the HPV Prevention Health Literacy Scale (HPV-HLS), for assessing HPV prevention health literacy among college students in Taiwan. The research was grounded in the context of HPV as a common sexually transmitted virus linked to various cancers, highlighting the importance of addressing health literacy in high-risk groups. A cross-sectional design was employed, involving 372 students from three universities in different regions of Taiwan. The scale was developed through qualitative interviews and literature review, then refined to 37 items following content validity and item analysis. Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses were conducted with 150 and 222 participants, respectively, to evaluate the scale's structure. The final scale included 21 items divided into two subscales: comprehension and evaluation of general information, and seeking information from health care professionals. The results showed a two-factor model explaining 60.30% of the total variation, with favorable goodness-of-fit indices (GFI = .81, CFI = .92, TLI = .91, RMSEA = .07, SRMR = .02). The average variance extracted (AVE) for the two factors were .56 and .64, with composite reliability (CR) values of .96 and .93, indicating strong convergent validity. The AVE exceeded the squared product-moment correlation, confirming good discriminant validity. Concurrent validity was supported by a correlation of .68 with the Mandarin Multidimensional Health Literacy Questionnaire (p < .001), and internal consistency was demonstrated with a Cronbach's α of .959. The authors concluded that the HPV-HLS is a reliable and valid tool for assessing HPV prevention health literacy, which can inform health care providers and educators in evaluating interventions to prevent HPV infection. The evidence is strong, with no reported limitations.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是一种常见的性传播病毒,与多种癌症有关。由于大学生属于高风险群体,了解他们关于HPV预防的健康素养至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 采用横断面研究设计,该量表在台湾北部两所大学和中部一所大学的372名大学生样本中进行了验证。
elements_zh.methods: 初始量表包含49个项目,来源于定性访谈和文献综述。在内容效度评估和项目分析后,量表被精简为37个项目。对150名参与者进行了探索性因子分析(EFA),随后对222名参与者进行了验证性因子分析(CFA)。评估了同时效度和内部一致性信度。
elements_zh.main_results: EFA的结果显示,一个双因素模型解释了总变异的60.30%,而CFA的结果表明拟合指标良好(GFI = .81,CFI = .92,TLI = .91,RMSEA = .07,SRMR = .02)。此外,两个因素的平均方差提取(AVE)分别为.56和.64,对应的组合信度(CR)值分别为.96和.93,表明具有良好的收敛效度。值得注意的是,AVE超过了相应因素的平方积矩相关系数,证实了良好的区分效度。最终的HPV-HLS量表包含21个项目,分为两个子量表:一般信息的理解与评估以及从医疗专业人员获取信息。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 经过严格的心理测量学测试,新开发的HPV-HLS表现出良好的信度和效度,使其成为评估大学生HPV预防健康素养的客观工具。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该HPV-HLS可由医疗保健提供者和教育工作者用于评估健康素养,并评估预防HPV感染的临床干预措施的有效性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 提供的证据未报告该研究的具体局限性。

papers.title_zh: 台湾大学生HPV预防健康素养量表的开发与心理测量学验证
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a common sexually transmitted virus associated with several types of cancer. Because college students are a high-risk group, understanding their health literacy with regard to HPV prevention is critical. However, no suitable measurement tools are currently available for this purpose. PURPOSE: In this study, an HPV Prevention Health Literacy Scale (HPV-HLS) was developed, and its reliability and validity were assessed. METHODS: A cross-sectional design was used, and the developed scale was validated on a sample of 372 college students from two universities in northern Taiwan and one university in central Taiwan. The initial scale comprised 49 items, developed from qualitative interviews and a literature review. After content validity assessment and item analysis, the scale was refined to 37 items. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) was conducted with 150 participants, followed by confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) with 222 participants. Concurrent validity and internal consistency reliability were assessed. Data were collected from November 2021 to December 2022. RESULTS: The results of the EFA revealed a two-factor model accounted for 60.30% of the total variation, and those of the CFA demonstrated favorable goodness-of-fit indices (GFI = .81, CFI = .92, TLI = .91, RMSEA = .07, and SRMR = .02). Moreover, the average variance extracted (AVE) for the two factors were .56 and .64, respectively, with corresponding composite reliability (CR) values of .96 and .93, indicating excellent convergent validity. Notably, the AVE surpassed the squared product-moment correlation of the corresponding factors, affirming good discriminant validity. The final iteration of the HPV-HLS comprised 21 items with two subscales: comprehension and evaluation of general information and seeking information from health care professionals. Concurrent validity was found between the proposed scale and the Mandarin Multidimensional Health Literacy Questionnaire ( r = .68, p < .001). The HPV-HLS demonstrated good internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .959). CONCLUSIONS/IMPLICATIONS FOR FUTURE PRACTICE: After rigorous psychometric testing, the newly developed HPV-HLS demonstrated excellent reliability and validity, establishing it as an objective tool for evaluating HPV prevention health literacy among college students. This HPV-HLS may be used by health care providers and educators to assess health literacy and evaluate the effectiveness of clinical interventions to prevent HPV infection.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)是一种常见的性传播病毒,与多种癌症有关。由于大学生属于高风险群体,了解他们关于HPV预防的健康素养至关重要。然而,目前尚无适合的测量工具可用于此目的。目的:本研究开发了HPV预防健康素养量表(HPV-HLS),并对其信度和效度进行了评估。方法:采用横断面研究设计,该量表在台湾北部两所大学和中部一所大学的372名大学生样本中进行了验证。初始量表包含49个项目,来源于定性访谈和文献综述。在内容效度评估和项目分析后,量表被精简为37个项目。对150名参与者进行了探索性因子分析(EFA),随后对222名参与者进行了验证性因子分析(CFA)。评估了同时效度和内部一致性信度。数据收集时间为2021年11月至2022年12月。结果:EFA的结果显示,一个双因素模型解释了总变异的60.30%,而CFA的结果表明拟合指标良好(GFI = .81,CFI = .92,TLI = .91,RMSEA = .07,SRMR = .02)。此外,两个因素的平均方差提取(AVE)分别为.56和.64,对应的组合信度(CR)值分别为.96和.93,表明具有良好的收敛效度。值得注意的是,AVE超过了相应因素的平方积矩相关系数,证实了良好的区分效度。最终的HPV-HLS量表包含21个项目,分为两个子量表:一般信息的理解与评估以及从医疗专业人员获取信息。该量表与中文多维健康素养问卷(r = .68,p < .001)之间表现出良好的同时效度。HPV-HLS表现出良好的内部一致性(Cronbach's α = .959)。结论/对未来实践的启示:经过严格的心理测量学测试,新开发的HPV-HLS表现出良好的信度和效度,使其成为评估大学生HPV预防健康素养的客观工具。该HPV-HLS可由医疗保健提供者和教育工作者用于评估健康素养,并评估预防HPV感染的临床干预措施的有效性。

papers.title: Cervicovaginal microbiome alterations across HPV infection
papers.abstract: Introduction The cervicovaginal microbiome is a proposed modifier of HPV-associated cervical disease, yet its relationship with viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST) remains incompletely understood. Methods This cross-sectional study characterized cervicovaginal microbiome composition and functional potential across HPV infection status, viral type categories (No HPV, HPV High Risk, HPV16, HPV18, HPV Other), cervical cytological grades, and CSTs in 311 non-pregnant women using whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing, integrated diversity analyses, MaAsLin2 differential abundance testing, and HUMAnN 3.0 functional pathway profiling. Results HPV-positive samples showed increased bacterial species richness, and a reciprocal Lactobacillus -to- Gardnerella dominance shift compared to HPV-negative samples. HPV Other showed the highest bacterial species richness and distinct taxonomic and predicted functional associations, including higher inferred abundance of siderophore- and lipopolysaccharide-biosynthesis pathways; however, overall species-level community composition did not differ significantly across HPV type groups. CST I and CST II exhibited compositional stability regardless of HPV status, while CST IV showed pronounced Lactobacillus depletion in HPV-positive women. LSIL was associated with lower Fannyhessea vaginae and Alloscardovia omnicolens abundance and higher Phocaeicola vulgatus abundance relative to NILM. Discussion These findings indicate that oncogenic potential and dysbiosis severity are not aligned, and that CST type modifies HPV–microbiome interactions.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the relationship between the cervicovaginal microbiome and HPV infection, particularly focusing on how viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST) might influence this relationship.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This cross-sectional study analyzed 311 non-pregnant women to characterize cervicovaginal microbiome composition and functional potential across HPV infection status, viral type categories, cervical cytological grades, and CSTs.
analysis.methods: The study used whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing, integrated diversity analyses, MaAsLin2 differential abundance testing, and HUMAnN 3.0 functional pathway profiling to assess microbiome composition and functional potential.
analysis.main_results: HPV-positive samples showed increased bacterial species richness and a reciprocal Lactobacillus-to-Gardnerella dominance shift compared to HPV-negative samples. HPV Other had the highest bacterial species richness and distinct taxonomic and predicted functional associations, including higher inferred abundance of siderophore- and lipopolysaccharide-biosynthesis pathways. CST IV showed pronounced Lactobacillus depletion in HPV-positive women. LSIL was associated with lower Fannyhessea vaginae and Alloscardovia omnicolens abundance and higher Phocaeicola vulgatus abundance relative to NILM.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that oncogenic potential and dysbiosis severity are not aligned, and that CST type modifies HPV–microbiome interactions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the microbiome's role in HPV infection and its potential implications for cervical disease progression, highlighting the importance of CST in modifying HPV–microbiome interactions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is cross-sectional, limiting causal inference, and the results are based on inferred functional pathways rather than direct measurements, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the cervicovaginal microbiome's relationship with HPV infection, focusing on viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST). Using metagenomic sequencing and functional pathway analysis, the research found that HPV-positive samples showed increased bacterial diversity and a shift in Lactobacillus-to-Gardnerella dominance. HPV Other was associated with the highest species richness and distinct functional profiles, while CST IV exhibited significant Lactobacillus depletion in HPV-positive women. LSIL was linked to reduced abundance of certain bacteria and increased Phocaeicola vulgatus. The authors suggest that CST type modifies HPV–microbiome interactions, indicating that oncogenic potential and dysbiosis severity may not be directly aligned. These findings could inform future studies on microbiome-based interventions for HPV-related cervical disease. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal conclusions, and the use of inferred functional pathways may affect the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨宫颈阴道微生物组与HPV感染之间的关系,特别是病毒类型异质性、细胞学分级以及社区状态类型(CST)如何影响这种关系。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本横断面研究分析了311名非妊娠女性,以特征化HPV感染状态、病毒类型分类、宫颈细胞学分级以及CSTs中的宫颈阴道微生物组组成和功能潜力。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究采用全基因组宏基因组测序、整合多样性分析、MaAsLin2差异丰度检验以及HUMAnN 3.0功能通路分析,以评估微生物组的组成和功能潜力。
elements_zh.main_results: HPV阳性样本表现出更高的细菌物种丰富度,并且与HPV阴性样本相比,乳酸杆菌与加德纳菌的主导地位发生了相互转换。其他HPV表现出最高的细菌物种丰富度,并具有独特的分类学和预测功能关联,包括铁载体和脂多糖合成通路的推断丰度较高。CST IV在HPV阳性女性中表现出显著的乳酸杆菌减少。LSIL与NILM相比,表现出更低的Fannyhessea vaginae和Alloscardovia omnicolens丰度,以及更高的Phocaeicola vulgatus丰度。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,致癌潜力和微生物失调严重程度并不一致,且CST类型可能调节HPV与微生物组的相互作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为理解微生物组在HPV感染中的作用及其对宫颈疾病进展的潜在影响提供了见解,强调了CST在调节HPV-微生物组相互作用中的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究为横断面研究,限制了因果推断的可能,且结果基于推断的功能通路而非直接测量,这可能影响证据的强度。

LSIL was associated with lower Fannyhessea vaginae and Alloscardovia omnicolens abundance and higher Phocaeicola vulgatus abundance relative to NILM.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that oncogenic potential and dysbiosis severity are not aligned, and that CST type modifies HPV–microbiome interactions.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the microbiome's role in HPV infection and its potential implications for cervical disease progression, highlighting the importance of CST in modifying HPV–microbiome interactions.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is cross-sectional, limiting causal inference, and the results are based on inferred functional pathways rather than direct measurements, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

papers.title_zh: HPV感染过程中宫颈阴道微生物组的变化
papers.source_body_en: Introduction The cervicovaginal microbiome is a proposed modifier of HPV-associated cervical disease, yet its relationship with viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST) remains incompletely understood. Methods This cross-sectional study characterized cervicovaginal microbiome composition and functional potential across HPV infection status, viral type categories (No HPV, HPV High Risk, HPV16, HPV18, HPV Other), cervical cytological grades, and CSTs in 311 non-pregnant women using whole-genome shotgun metagenomic sequencing, integrated diversity analyses, MaAsLin2 differential abundance testing, and HUMAnN 3.0 functional pathway profiling. Results HPV-positive samples showed increased bacterial species richness, and a reciprocal Lactobacillus -to- Gardnerella dominance shift compared to HPV-negative samples. HPV Other showed the highest bacterial species richness and distinct taxonomic and predicted functional associations, including higher inferred abundance of siderophore- and lipopolysaccharide-biosynthesis pathways; however, overall species-level community composition did not differ significantly across HPV type groups. CST I and CST II exhibited compositional stability regardless of HPV status, while CST IV showed pronounced Lactobacillus depletion in HPV-positive women. LSIL was associated with lower Fannyhessea vaginae and Alloscardovia omnicolens abundance and higher Phocaeicola vulgatus abundance relative to NILM. Discussion These findings indicate that oncogenic potential and dysbiosis severity are not aligned, and that CST type modifies HPV–microbiome interactions.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言 宫颈阴道微生物组被认为是影响HPV相关宫颈疾病的一个潜在调节因素,但其与病毒类型异质性、细胞学分级以及社区状态类型(CST)之间的关系仍不完全明确。方法 本横断面研究利用全基因组宏基因组测序、整合多样性分析、MaAsLin2差异丰度检验以及HUMAnN 3.0功能通路分析,对311名非妊娠女性在HPV感染状态、病毒类型分类(无HPV、高危型HPV、HPV16、HPV18、其他HPV)、宫颈细胞学分级以及CSTs中的宫颈阴道微生物组组成和功能潜力进行了特征分析。结果 HPV阳性样本表现出更高的细菌物种丰富度,并且与HPV阴性样本相比,乳酸杆菌与加德纳菌的主导地位发生了相互转换。其他HPV表现出最高的细菌物种丰富度,并具有独特的分类学和预测功能关联,包括铁载体和脂多糖合成通路的推断丰度较高;然而,总体物种水平的微生物组组成在不同HPV类型组之间没有显著差异。CST I和CST II无论HPV状态如何都表现出组成稳定性,而CST IV在HPV阳性女性中表现出显著的乳酸杆菌减少。LSIL与NILM相比,表现出更低的Fannyhessea vaginae和Alloscardovia omnicolens丰度,以及更高的Phocaeicola vulgatus丰度。讨论 这些发现表明,致癌潜力和微生物失调严重程度并不一致,且CST类型可能调节HPV与微生物组的相互作用。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨宫颈阴道微生物组与HPV感染之间的关系,特别是病毒类型异质性、细胞学分级以及社区状态类型(CST)如何影响这种关系。

analysis_zh.methods: 本研究采用全基因组宏基因组测序、整合多样性分析、MaAsLin2差异丰度检验以及HUMAnN 3.0功能通路分析,以评估微生物组的组成和功能潜力。
analysis_zh.main_results: HPV阳性样本表现出更高的细菌物种丰富度,并且与HPV阴性样本相比,乳酸杆菌与加德纳菌的主导地位发生了相互转换。其他HPV表现出最高的细菌物种丰富度,并具有独特的分类学和预测功能关联,包括铁载体和脂多糖合成通路的推断丰度较高。CST IV在HPV阳性女性中表现出显著的乳酸杆菌减少。LSIL与NILM相比,表现出更低的Fannyhessea vaginae和Alloscardovia omnicolens丰度,以及更高的Phocaeicola vulgatus丰度。

analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为理解微生物组在HPV感染中的作用及其对宫颈疾病进展的潜在影响提供了见解,强调了CST在调节HPV-微生物组相互作用中的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究为横断面研究,限制了因果推断的可能,且结果基于推断的功能通路而非直接测量,这可能影响证据的强度。

papers.title: Sexual Function and Psychological Distress Across Surveillance, Colposcopy, and LEEP in Women with a History of High-Risk HPV Positivity: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: High-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) positivity and its management may affect sexual function and psychological well-being, yet whether this burden differs across the successive steps of cervical management is unclear. We compared sexual function, quality of life, and psychological distress across three management steps—surveillance, colposcopy, and loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). Methods: In this single-center cross-sectional study, 302 reproductive-age women with a history of hrHPV positivity (surveillance, n = 50; colposcopy, n = 177; LEEP, n = 75) completed the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), WHOQOL-BREF, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Groups were compared with Kruskal–Wallis and chi-square tests; FSFI total was modelled by multivariable linear regression and FSFI-defined dysfunction by logistic regression. Results: No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in FSFI total (medians 23.8/25.2/24.5; p = 0.897), FSFI subdomains, HADS, or WHOQOL domains; FSFI-defined dysfunction was frequent across groups, with no statistically significant between-group difference (59–67%). No statistically significant association between management pathway and FSFI was observed in the adjusted models (LEEP vs. surveillance B = −0.63, 95% CI −4.68 to +3.42). Depressive symptoms—but not anxiety—were associated with FSFI-defined dysfunction (per HADS-D point, OR = 1.14, 95% CI 1.03–1.26, p = 0.009), whereas the association with continuous FSFI was not significant (B = −0.37, p = 0.064). Marital status was the strongest overall correlate. analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study investigated the impact of high-risk HPV management steps—surveillance, colposcopy, and LEEP—on sexual function and psychological distress in 302 reproductive-age women. Participants completed validated questionnaires assessing sexual function, quality of life, and psychological well-being. We compared sexual function, quality of life, and psychological distress across three management steps—surveillance, colposcopy, and loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). Methods: In this single-center cross-sectional study, 302 reproductive-age women with a history of hrHPV positivity (surveillance, n = 50; colposcopy, n = 177; LEEP, n = 75) completed the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), WHOQOL-BREF, and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS). Groups were compared with Kruskal–Wallis and chi-square tests; FSFI total was modelled by multivariable linear regression and FSFI-defined dysfunction by logistic regression. Results: No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in FSFI total (medians 23.8/25.2/24.5; p = 0.897), FSFI subdomains, HADS, or WHOQOL domains; FSFI-defined dysfunction was frequent across groups, with no statistically significant between-group difference (59–67%). No statistically significant association between management pathway and FSFI was observed in the adjusted models (LEEP vs. surveillance B = −0.63, 95% CI −4.68 to +3.42). Depressive symptoms—but not anxiety—were associated with FSFI-defined dysfunction (per HADS-D point, OR = 1.14, 95% CI 1.03–1.26, p = 0.009), whereas the association with continuous FSFI was not significant (B = −0.37, p = 0.064). Marital status was the strongest overall correlate. Conclusions: Across surveillance, colposcopy, and LEEP, sexual function did not differ significantly between management groups at the time of assessment, and, in exploratory analyses, depressive symptoms showed the most consistent association with sexual dysfunction. These findings highlight the potential relevance of psychosocial and relational context in the psychosexual care of women with a history of hrHPV positivity, although prospective studies are needed before specific screening or counselling recommendations can be made.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨在有高危型HPV阳性史的女性中,宫颈管理的各个阶段是否对性功能和心理压力负担产生差异。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为单中心横断面研究,纳入了302名有高危型HPV阳性史的育龄女性,分为三组:监测组(n = 50)、阴道镜检查组(n = 177)和环形电切术(LEEP)组(n = 75)。
analysis_zh.methods: 参与者完成了女性性功能指数(FSFI)、WHOQOL-BREF量表和医院焦虑抑郁量表(HADS)。使用Kruskal–Wallis检验和卡方检验比较各组;FSFI总分通过多变量线性回归建模,FSFI定义的功能障碍通过逻辑回归分析。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,管理组之间的性功能无显著差异,而在探索性分析中,抑郁症状与性功能障碍表现出最一致的关联。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,在有高危型HPV阳性史的女性心理性健康护理中,应考虑心理社会和关系因素,强调了对筛查和咨询策略进行进一步研究的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究为横断面研究,限制了因果推论的可能,且调整模型中未发现管理路径与FSFI之间的显著关联,表明证据强度中等。

papers.title: AI Chatbot Use for Human Papillomavirus Vaccine Literacy in Japan
papers.abstract: Importance Persistent misinformation and low confidence impede human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccine uptake in Japan. Artificial intelligence (AI)–driven conversational agents may provide scalable vaccine education, but randomized evidence for HPV vaccine communication remains limited. Objective To determine whether an AI-driven HPV vaccine chatbot improves caregiver HPV vaccine literacy compared with a government leaflet. Design, Setting, and Participants Parallel-group randomized clinical trial (RCT) conducted through a national research panel of female caregivers in Japan with unvaccinated daughters aged 12 to 18 years from November 30 to December 27, 2024, with 2-week follow-up. Interventions Participants were randomized 1:1 to an AI-driven HPV vaccine chatbot or standard government HPV vaccine leaflet. Main outcomes and measures The primary outcome was an HPV vaccine literacy, evaluated immediately after intervention to estimate immediate intervention efficacy and evaluated at 2-week follow-up to estimate durability. HPV vaccine literacy was measured using 7 factual questions about HPV and HPV vaccination; scores are shown on a 0 to 7 scale, with higher scores indicating more correct responses.The secondary outcome was decision to vaccinate at 2-week follow-up. Results Among 848 randomized participants, 704 of 841 (83.7%) were included in the immediate modified intention-to-treat (mITT) analysis (353 chatbot, 351 leaflet) and 477 of 841 (56.7%) in the mITT analysis at 2 weeks (237 chatbot, 240 leaflet). A total of 447 of 703 participants (63.6%) were aged 40 to 49 years and had college or university education (472 of 703 participants [67.1%]). Immediately after the intervention, analysis of covariance-adjusted literacy was higher with the chatbot (adjusted mean difference, 0.30 points on the 0 to 7 scale; 95% CI, 0.18-0.43 points; P < .001). At the 2-week durability assessment, mean (SD) literacy increased by 0.40 (1.21) with the chatbot vs 0.28 (1.13) points with the leaflet; adjusted literacy again favored the chatbot (adjusted mean difference, 0.30 points; 95% CI, 0.13-0.47; P < .001). At 2 weeks, caregivers’ vaccination decisions did not differ between groups (102 of 253 participants [40.3%] vs 103 of 260 participants [39.6%]; adjusted odds ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.41 to 1.33; P = .31). Conclusions and Relevance In this RCT of female caregivers in Japan, an AI-driven HPV vaccine chatbot produced higher adjusted HPV vaccine literacy than a government leaflet immediately after intervention and at 2-week follow-up, without a measurable short-term effect on vaccination decision. Conversational AI may complement official materials and health care professional recommendations. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06702423

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在通过评估AI驱动的HPV疫苗接种聊天机器人与政府传单相比的效果,解决日本HPV疫苗接种率提升过程中持续的错误信息和低信任度的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在一项针对日本12至18岁未接种HPV疫苗的女儿的母亲的平行组随机临床试验中,比较了聊天机器人组和传单组在干预后立即和2周随访时的HPV疫苗接种知识的持续性。
elements_zh.methods: 通过7个关于HPV及其疫苗接种的客观问题来测量HPV疫苗接种知识,主要结果在干预后立即和2周随访时进行评估。次要结果是在2周随访时的疫苗接种决定。
elements_zh.main_results: 聊天机器人组在干预后立即和2周随访时均显示出比传单组更高的HPV疫苗接种知识,但对疫苗接种决定没有显著影响。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究得出结论,AI驱动的HPV疫苗接种聊天机器人比政府传单更能有效提升HPV疫苗接种知识,其效果可持续至2周,但对疫苗接种决定没有显著影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,对话式AI可能在提升HPV疫苗接种知识方面补充官方材料和医疗专业人员的建议。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性包括样本量较小和随访时间较短,这可能影响研究结果的普遍性。

news.content_title: PDS Biotech Announces Publication of VERSATILE-002 Phase 2 Clinical Trial Results of PDS0101 with pembrolizumab in HPV16-Positive Recurrent and/or Metastatic (R/M) Head and Neck Cancer in JAMA Oncology
news.content: 39.3 months median overall survival in first-line (1L) R/M immune checkpoint inhibitor naïve patients Company continues to prioritize PDS0301 in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) while pursuing partnership strategy for PDS0101 PRINCETON, N.J., Sept. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- PDS Biotechnology Corporation (Nasdaq: PDSB) ("PDS Biotech” or the "Company”), a late-stage immunotherapy company focused on transforming how the immune system targets and kills cancers, today announced the publication of results from a Phase 2 trial evaluating PDS0101, its HPV16-targeted immunotherapy, in combination with pembrolizumab in the September 17, 2026, issue of JAMA Oncology , a peer reviewed journal of the American Medical Association . The data were published in an article titled " VERSATILE-002 - A Phase 2 Study of PDS0101 HPV16-targeted T Cell Immunotherapy and Pembrolizumab Combination in HPV16-Positive Recurrent/Metastatic Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Nonrandomized Clinical Trial . ” Key findings Get the latest news delivered to your inbox Sign up for The Manila Times newsletters By signing up with an email address, I acknowledge that I have read and agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy . 62.3% of the ICI-naïve participants in the mITT cohort (n = 53) had low CPS of 1-19, and 37.7% had high CPS ≥ 20. In the overall CPS ≥ 1 population, the mOS was 39.3 months (95% CI, 23.9 to NE); The best published result with standard of care pembrolizumab or pembrolizumab + chemotherapy is 17.9 months 1. Objective response rate (ORR) for CPS ≥ 1 was 36% of which 5/53 were complete responders by investigator review and 34% of which 6/53 were complete responders by central review. The published ORR for the overall population with CPS ≥ 1 when treated with standard of care pembrolizumab is 19%2. The treatment was well-tolerated with 13.8% Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs), 1 Grade 4 event one year after PDS0101 therapy, and no Grade 5 TRAEs. The published safety profile for the overall population with CPS ≥ 1 when treated with standard of care pembrolizumab reports 17% Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs2. VERSATILE-002 was an open-label, non-randomized phase 2 trial performed at twenty-six oncology centers across the US, UK and Ireland. Eighty-eight patients with histologically confirmed R/M HPV16-positive diseases were enrolled in the study; 87 received treatment and comprised the safety population; 75 were in the modified Intention-to-Treat (mITT) population used for efficacy analyses: 53 ICI-naïve with PD-L1 CPS ≥1, 22 ICI-resistant (Mean age = 64.5 years, 94.7% male, 92.0% White). The trial was led by Dr. Jared Weiss, MD, of the Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill, NC, and was performed to determine the efficacy and safety of PDS0101, in combination with pembrolizumab in participants with HPV16-positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (R/M HNSCC), with separate evaluation of immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-naïve and -resistant cohorts. "We’re very pleased with the publication of the Phase 2 clinical results of the VERSATILE-002 clinical trial in a leading peer reviewed oncology journal,” said Dr. Kirk Shepard, M.D., Chief Medical Officer of PDS Biotech. "These results support the durable clinical effect of PDS0101, consistent with promising survival outcomes reported in two other recently published studies, the IMMUNOCERV study, and the NCI-led study in HPV16-positive recurrent and/or metastatic cancers. We believe PDS0101 has the potential to bring new hope to the rapidly growing population of HPV16-positive head and neck cancer patients.” The Company recently announced the initial closing of a PIPE financing of up to $22.3 million led by Nant Capital, alongside an agreement granting NantWorks, LLC, an affiliate of Nant Capital, a one-year exclusive right to negotiate an exclusive license to PDS0101. *No head-to-head trials have been performed. 1 Licitra L et al, J Clin Oncol; 2026 Apr 20;44(12):1098-1107.doi: 10.1200/JCO-25-00570. Epub 2026 Mar 12 2 Harrington, KJ et al. J Clin Oncol. 2022;41:790-802. https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.21.02508 . About PDS Biotechnology PDS Biotechnology is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing targeted immunotherapies for cancer. PDS Biotechnology owns the Versamune® cancer vaccine platform, including PDS0101, which has been evaluated in HPV16-positive cancers. The Company intends to pursue strategic partnerships or other externally funded opportunities for the Phase 3 development of PDS0101. The Company’s lead development program, PDS0301 (also referred to as PDS01ADC & NHS-IL12), is an investigational tumor-targeted interleukin-12 (IL-12) immunocytokine designed to deliver IL-12 preferentially to the tumor microenvironment, with the goal of enhancing anti-tumor immune activity while limiting systemic exposure. PDS0301 has been clinically evaluated across multiple solid tumors, including metastatic colorectal cancer and prostate cancer. The Company is focused on advancing PDS0301 in indications where its tumor-targeted mechanism may help address and overcome mechanisms of resistance to immunotherapy. Moe also serves as Head of Research at CliniBiz and Chief Data Scientist at Annex Clinical Corporation. Adaptive Clinical Trial Design Adaptive Trial Design Addiction Psychiatry AI in Clinical Trials alcohol use disorder Alzheimer's Disease Article Clinical Operations Clinical Research Clinical Trial Design Clinical Trial Operations Clinical Trial Ops Brief Clinical Trials CLINOPS WATCHDOG CNS Drug Development CNS Trials Conference Coverage Decentralized Clinical Trials Digital Health Technologies dual diagnosis eClinical Tech News eClinical Technology EMA Executive Interviews FDA Enforcement FDA Guidance FDA Real-World Evidence FDA Regulation FDA Regulatory Strategy FDA Warning Letter GCP Compliance GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Ketamine Therapy Oncology Trials Opinion Parkinson's Disease Platform Trials Psilocybin MDMA Psychedelic Clinical Trials PSYCH PULSE Real-World Evidence site activation Site Operations study startup Treatment-Resistant Depression Search for:Search Button Articles Conference Coverage Executive Interviews News CliniCast News PDS0101 Plus Pembrolizumab Shows 39.3-Month Survival in HPV16 Head and Neck Cancer By Jon Napitupulu September 24, 2026 A 39.3-month median overall survival in checkpoint-inhibitor-naïve patients is the kind of number that demands attention in recurrent or metastatic head and neck cancer, where outcomes have historically been grim. PDS Biotechnology announced September 22 that results from its VERSATILE-002 Phase 2 trial are now published in JAMA Oncology, putting the data into the peer-reviewed record rather than the conference-abstract circuit where clinical claims often circulate without full scrutiny. The trial tested PDS0101, an HPV16-targeted immunotherapy, combined with pembrolizumab in patients with HPV16-positive recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma. The 39.3-month median overall survival figure comes from the modified intention-to-treat population with a PD-L1 Combined Positive Score of at least 1, the patients most likely to respond to checkpoint inhibition. That population is also the commercial sweet spot, since PD-L1 CPS guides pembrolizumab dosing decisions in standard practice, and a survival signal this durable in a combination regimen will draw direct comparisons to pembrolizumab monotherapy benchmarks already in the literature. Publication in a peer-reviewed journal matters beyond prestige. Payers, guideline committees, and potential partners weigh journal-level evidence differently than data presented at a conference or posted on ClinicalTrials.gov. The JAMA Oncology appearance gives VERSATILE-002 the citation permanence that supports a biologics license application narrative and gives investigators a citable reference when designing follow-on studies or combination arms. PDS Biotechnology is a small company, and having this dataset anchored in a high-impact journal strengthens the hand of anyone evaluating a licensing or co-development conversation. The trial was Phase 2, so the survival figure carries the usual caveats about sample size and the absence of a randomized comparator arm. The next concrete marker is whether PDS Biotechnology uses the JAMA Oncology publication as the scientific foundation to advance toward a registrational study, and whether a larger partner moves first to claim the HPV16-targeted combination space in head and neck cancer. supplementary_news.content: PDS Biotech's HPV16 cancer immunotherapy posts 39.3-month survival in JAMA Oncology ● 3 days ago What happened? On 2026-09-22, PDS Biotechnology announced the publication of final survival data from its Phase ️2 VERSATILE-002 trial in JAMA Oncology. The study evaluated PDS0101, an experimental immunotherapy designed to activate T cells against tumours caused by the HPV16 virus, combined with pembrolizumab(Keytruda(, in people with recurrent or metastatic head-and-neck cancer. In patients without prior checkpoint-inhibitor therapy whose tumours expressed the PD-L1 protein(CPS≥1(, median overall survival was 39.3 months——far longer than the roughly ️17.9-month benchmark cited for standard pembrolizumab-based care, though comparisons across different trials need caution. Why it matters: Head-and-neck cancer that returns or spreads is hard to treat,ands survival beyond three years in this setting is unusually long. These results were published in the ️2026-09-17 issue of JAMA Oncology,and are among the strongest reported for HPV16-positive patients. PDS0101 works by training the immune system to attack cancer cells displaying viral proteins, offering a potentially durable response for patients whose tumours are driven by HPV16, which accounts for a sizeable share of head-and-neck cancers. The company says the data support its goal of bringing PDS0101 to patients with limited options,and it is engaging with regulators on next steps toward approval. Read more: PDS via BioSpace, 2026-09-22 · Targeted Oncology, 2026-09-22

Kovina Therapeutics Awarded $2.3 Million NCI Grant to Advance First-in-Class HPV Cancer Therapy Directly Targeting E6 Business Wire Thu, September 24, 2026 at 6:00 AM MDT 3 min read Direct-to-Phase II SBIR award supports IND-enabling development of Kovina's lead oral small molecule program INDIANAPOLIS, September 24, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Kovina Therapeutics Inc., a biotechnology company developing first-in-class small molecule therapeutics targeting the Human Papillomavirus (HPV) E6 oncoprotein, today announced a $2.3 million Direct-to-Phase II Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) award from the National Cancer Institute (NCI). The two-year award will support IND-enabling development of Kovina's lead oral small molecule program for HPV-driven cancers. The award follows Kovina's recent publication in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS) validating direct pharmacologic targeting of HPV E6. The research demonstrated restoration of p53 tumor suppressor activity, selective killing of HPV-positive cancer cells and tumor growth inhibition in HPV-positive preclinical models. "This award comes at an important point for Kovina as we move from compelling preclinical science into formal development," said Kristin Sherman, Chief Executive Officer of Kovina Therapeutics. "Together with our recent PNAS publication, the NCI support gives us significant momentum as we advance our lead program through IND-enabling development and toward the clinic." HPV E6 is a viral oncoprotein that degrades the tumor suppressor p53 and is required for the survival of HPV-positive cancer cells. Kovina's small molecules are designed to inhibit E6 and restore p53 function, offering a targeted approach to the underlying mechanism of these cancers. The NCI award will support key development activities, including CMC, IND-enabling pharmacology and toxicology, and other studies required to support an Investigational New Drug application. "HPV E6 has long been recognized as a compelling cancer target but directly inhibiting it with a small molecule has been challenging," said Elliot Androphy, M.D., Founder and Chief Scientific Officer of Kovina Therapeutics. "Our work demonstrates that E6 can be specifically targeted, restoring p53 and selectively killing HPV-positive cancer cells. This gives us a strong foundation for translating the biology into a new therapeutic approach." Despite preventive vaccines, HPV causes an estimated 39,300 cancers each year in the United States, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, including cervical and head and neck cancers. By directly targeting HPV E6, Kovina's approach has the potential to treat a spectrum of HPV-associated disease, from premalignant disease to invasive cancers. Story Continues About Kovina Therapeutics Kovina Therapeutics is a preclinical-stage biotechnology company developing first-in-class small molecule therapeutics targeting HPV E6, an oncoprotein essential to the development and survival of HPV-associated cancers and premalignant disease. The company is advancing its lead oral program toward clinical development. To learn more, visit www.kovina.com. About the NCI SBIR Award Research reported in this press release is supported by the National Cancer Institute of the National Institutes of Health under Award Number R44CA302154. The content is solely the responsibility of Kovina Therapeutics and does not necessarily represent the official views of the National Institutes of Health. 秋季新学期已经拉开帷幕,在做好季节性传染病防控的同时,适龄女孩HPV疫苗接种同样值得家长列入新学期健康计划。宫颈癌是目前世界上唯一病因明确的恶性肿瘤,而接种HPV疫苗,正是从源头阻断HPV感染最经济、最有效的手段。江苏省正通过“国家免疫规划免费接种+地方惠民活动减免”双轨并行模式,为适龄人群提供多元化的HPV疫苗接种选择。 小年龄段接种免疫效果更好 早预防早保护 宫颈癌是严重威胁女性健康的公共卫生问题。几乎所有的宫颈癌(99%以上)都与高危型HPV持续感染密切相关。在中国,常见的感染型别为HPV52、16、58。近年来,我国宫颈癌发病率呈上升趋势,宫颈癌发病年龄呈现年轻化趋势,部分病例甚至出现在20多岁未育女性中。 同时,宫颈癌是一种可以预防的癌症,2023年中国《子宫颈癌综合防控指南(第2版)》提出了三级预防策略,其中,一级预防的主要措施包括开展健康教育和接种预防性HPV疫苗;二级预防强调早筛早诊;三级预防则是对已确诊的宫颈癌患者进行规范治疗。 世界卫生组织明确推荐:9-14岁未发生性行为的女孩是首要接种人群。从感染风险看,HPV主要通过性行为传播,首次性行为前接种可获得更好的保护效果;从免疫效果看,9-14岁女孩接种后产生的抗体水平是15岁以上人群的2倍以上,保护效果可持续至少10年。 自2023年起,江苏省把“为适龄女生免费接种HPV疫苗”纳入省政府民生实事项目,按照“知情、同意、自愿”的原则,为全省初一女生免费接种国产双价HPV疫苗。此后,HPV疫苗也被纳入国家免疫规划。我国将13周岁女孩确定为HPV疫苗免费接种人群,是综合考虑保护效果、成本效益和可操作性而确定的最优方案。 目前,除免疫规划疫苗为适龄女孩免费提供外,还有多种非免疫规划HPV疫苗供受种者自愿、自费接种。如适龄女孩已按照相应价次疫苗的免疫程序完成全程接种,同样视为完成国家HPV疫苗免疫规划接种。 部分年龄段减免将截止 抓紧9月30日窗口接种 从年龄来看,中国女性HPV感染率按年龄呈“双峰”分布:第一个高峰在17-24岁,这与年轻女性处于性活跃初期有关;第二个高峰在40-44岁。大年龄段女性的免疫功能可能会随年龄增加而下降,对新发和既往感染的清除能力也会随之下降,从而可能更容易发生持续感染,所以接种HPV疫苗对成年女性也十分有必要。 在全球范围内,90%的男性在其一生中至少感染一次HPV,男性生殖器HPV的感染率实际上高于女性,男性感染HPV后可能导致肛门癌、阴茎癌、口咽癌和尖锐湿疣。HPV疫苗不仅可以预防女性宫颈癌,还可以预防男性感染HPV引起的肛门癌和生殖器疣等。 由中华医学会妇科肿瘤学分会等七个学会共同制定发布的《预防性人乳头瘤病毒疫苗中国临床应用指南(2025版)》,优先推荐9-26岁女性接种HPV疫苗,其中9-14岁女孩是重点人群;同时推荐27-45岁女性和9-26岁男性接种。 为落实《“健康中国2030”规划纲要》和《江苏省加速消除宫颈癌行动计划实施方案(2023—2030年)》等文件要求,江苏省多地推出了适龄人群HPV疫苗接种惠民活动,并且将男性也纳入惠民范围,满足了更多样化的健康防护需求。 值得关注的是,根据江苏多地发布的信息,从2026年10月1日起,进口九价HPV疫苗惠民减免接种活动将调整,惠民人群范围也有所调整。其中,9-14岁女性、18-26岁女性及18-26岁男性接种进口九价HPV疫苗,可减免一针费用。其中,9-14岁女生只需接种2剂次,第二剂次免费。惠民活动首针接种结束时间延长至2027年12月31日。自2026年10月1日起,15-17周岁女性、35-45周岁女性、16-17周岁男性不再纳入进口九价HPV疫苗惠民范围。上述人群如要享受惠民减免,须在2026年9月30日前完成首针接种,且在2027年3月31日前完成全程接种。因各区县惠民活动起止时间可能不一致,具体以当地出台接种活动细则为准。 开设学生专场、周末门诊 江苏持续优化接种服务 江苏省高度重视HPV疫苗接种工作,为提升接种可及性,江苏省各地正积极探索优化接种服务新模式。二级以上公立医院、乡镇卫生院和社区卫生服务中心预防接种门诊均提供周末疫苗接种服务。江苏多地还利用节假日和周末门诊开设学生接种专场,家长不用请假,孩子也不耽误学习,接种意愿和满意度更高,适龄女生可根据学校通知前往指定接种门诊,或通过“江苏预防接种”APP 预约就近接种。其他居民同样可通过APP预约,或咨询当地接种门诊。同时,为提高公众科学认知,江苏省聘请省人民医院妇科主任程文俊和省广电总台主持人胡馨尹担任“预防接种公益宣传大使”,为HPV疫苗接种等预防接种工作提供权威专业科普指导。 针对部分家长担心的“孩子年龄还小,应等成年后再接种”等观点,专家指出,这其实是一个认知误区。HPV疫苗属于预防性疫苗,在病毒暴露前接种能够提前筑牢防护屏障,等到成年再打,反而错过了最佳防护期,保护效果会大打折扣。9-14岁女孩只需接种2剂次,即可获得充分保护,比15岁以上人群少打一针。 无论从免疫效果、时间还是经济成本考量,早接种都是最优选择。 图片来源 视觉中国 校对 陶善工 要闻 更多>>
